story.summaryEn: As Formula 1 announced its 24-race 2027 calendar, the most intriguing novelty is the Monaco Grand Prix receiving a sprint format, and Motorsport.com's writers weigh up whether that is a good idea or just bonkers. Some argue it disrupts the DNA of the Monaco weekend, while others believe F1 could be braver with its sprint format.
detailZh: 摩纳哥F1冲刺赛：好主意还是疯狂之举？我们的记者各抒己见
随着F1公布2027年24站赛历，最引人关注的新变化是摩纳哥大奖赛将采用冲刺赛制。这是好主意还是疯狂之举？我们的记者权衡利弊。
F1长期以来一直计划将目前每年六个冲刺赛周末的数量进一步增加，因为该赛制能让推广方向付费观众提供更多有意义的赛道内容，使冲刺赛周末成为值得花钱的卖点。数据显示，相比无意义的练习赛，车迷也更频繁地收看冲刺赛，尽管冲刺赛制本身仍引发争议。
F1将冲刺赛制应用于摩纳哥这条列队行驶的赛道，是否有些过火了？我们的记者给出他们的判断。
两场排位赛破坏了摩纳哥周末逐步升温的DNA——Ronald Vording
我必须承认，我仍然不是冲刺赛制的最大粉丝，尽管也许不像几年前那样强烈反对了。我想人总会习惯一切，但如果让我选择，我仍然更偏爱传统的比赛周末——部分原因也是在赛道上文字媒体工作流程的问题。
尽管如此，冲刺赛周末的商业好处是显而易见的。周五和周六对推广方来说变得更有吸引力，因为买票的人能看到更多真正有意义的环节。当然，F1管理层说这是基于数据显示车迷有多喜欢它，但大家都知道这并不能说明全部。
在摩纳哥举办冲刺赛似乎从商业上并无必要，但在这方面重要的是要记住，冲刺赛周末不仅仅是两场比赛。从逻辑上讲，这个赛制也意味着两场排位赛，而这正是让摩纳哥天平倾斜的原因。从这个角度看，明年我们将两次看到摩纳哥所能提供的最精彩内容。
你可能会说这听起来不错，因为摩纳哥的排位赛总是让车迷屏息凝神。但它带走了摩纳哥周末的一些魅力。毕竟，摩纳哥比赛周末的全部意义在于逐步推向绝对高潮，那是F1赛季最精彩的时刻之一。它关乎看着车手在每次练习赛中一点点逼近护墙，直到周六下午的那一个巅峰时刻。
后者在赛道边行走时也清晰可见——这在摩纳哥是无与伦比的。虽然车手在第一次练习赛中故意留出一些余量，但一天后——在第三次练习赛接近尾声时——你会越来越多地看到他们在Piscine和Tabac等地方寻找极限。这是在与风险调情，是在建立信心与想要太多太快之间的平衡。而这种平衡可能会出错——问问维斯塔潘就知道了，他在2018年最后一次练习赛中撞车，不得不驾驶一辆本可能获胜的赛车错过排位赛。
一场接一场地逐步构建摩纳哥周末，在周六达到那一个巅峰，对车手来说是一门艺术，对观众来说是一种享受。而正是这种动态现在正在改变。明年，由于上午有冲刺赛，通往常规排位赛的铺垫将完全不同，同时也引发了车手愿意承担多大风险的问题，因为周六下午对周末的结果至关重要。
摩纳哥的两场排位赛无疑将非常精彩，但这改变了摩纳哥周末的DNA以及车手构建它的方式——我不确定我内心中的纯粹主义者一定需要这种改变。
F1可以在冲刺赛制上更大胆，考虑倒序发车——Oleg Karpov
制定F1赛历不是一件小事，虽然在现代世界抨击当权者是一种好习惯，但他们实际上做得不错。F1的赛程很好地混合了历史悠久的赛道——蒙扎、斯帕和摩纳哥等仍然占有一席之地——以及像拉斯维加斯和迈阿密这样独特的新赛道，因为这项世界锦标赛正尽力利用其在美国的增长。
马德里也是不错的一步，在欧洲首都之一建街道赛道的想法很好——遗憾的是赛道本身没有达到预期。但如果当地组织者真正努力解决超车问题，未来仍可能取得成功。
加拿大大奖赛也将在2027年举办冲刺赛周末
总体而言，2027年赛历做得很好，抱怨比赛数量增加也有点无意义，毕竟与不久前的过去相比确实增加了。但作为与其他重大体育赛事竞争的全球娱乐产业，这一步是不可避免的。比赛数量进一步增加可能也是如此。
虽然我理解计划必须是进一步增加冲刺赛数量——甚至可能让每场大奖赛都设冲刺赛——但该赛制是否正确仍存疑问。至少在我看来，F1似乎可以更大胆一些，提供一些不同于“迷你大奖赛”的东西，后者只是被塞进一个更大赛事的日程中。本质上，以目前的状态，它除了稍微预览一下我们即将在主赛中看到的内容外，并没有提供太多东西。
这种赛制还确保那些得分最多的人又有机会得更多分，进一步拉大与其他车手的差距——那为什么不干脆让这项赛事属于小车队，给他们一个机会呢？是的，你猜对了，我说的是倒序发车——在我看来，至少可以考虑将赛制颠倒过来，取消额外的排位赛，让发车顺序按积分榜顺序——倒序排列。
我们会看到凯迪拉克和威廉姆斯的车手在这样的比赛中努力多抢几分，这肯定会增加另一个悬念：积分榜领先者从后排起步还能上升多少位？
人为吗？当然。但让专门制造的车辆在赛道上绕圈本身也并不是很自然的事。这不会触及大奖赛赛制本身，最大积分仍归主赛，但至少能提供一些不同的东西，带来全新的悬念。
F1 2027年赛历恰恰证明冲刺赛制需要改革
不久前我为姊妹网站Autosport写了一篇专栏，主张对冲刺赛制进行改革，而看到2027年选出的10个冲刺赛举办地，只会让我更加坚定这个想法。
长话短说，如果你打算每年举办10场冲刺赛，它就需要与主赛有不同的面貌。策略变化是赛道动作和超车的主要驱动力，而一场没有进站短程比赛几乎提供不了这些。
为什么不在冲刺赛周末尝试单圈排位淘汰赛，并按积分榜顺序进行呢？这意味着，按目前情况，安东内利会在赛道条件不是最好时第一个出场，而阿斯顿马丁和凯迪拉克最后出场。
这不像完全倒序发车那样人为，我出于体育原因强烈反对后者。但这是一种更温和地增加悬念的方式，同时仍让车手和车队发挥作用。而且该赛制只适用于冲刺赛发车顺序，保留了大奖赛本身的纯粹性。
单圈排位赛制能否帮助F1的冲刺赛脱颖而出？
就摩纳哥而言，对我来说这感觉像是F1在承认大奖赛作为赛车比赛而非美化巡游方面举白旗。很明显摩纳哥大奖赛不会消失，而且考虑到后勤限制，赛道也将长期保持原样。
2025年可怕的两次进站实验没有成功，所以感觉F1高层已经放弃让大奖赛变得有竞争力，转而倾向于摩纳哥最擅长的事情，即提供两场排位赛而非一场。
从推广角度看这是可以理解的，但如果我们只是接受F1的一些比赛事先就被判定为无望，那感觉就是根本上有问题。
增加更多冲刺赛是好主意吗？F1如何改进赛制？在下方发表你的看法
detailEn: Is a Monaco F1 sprint a good idea or just mad? Our writers have their say

As Formula 1 announced its 24-race 2027 calendar, the most intriguing novelty is the Monaco Grand Prix receiving a sprint format. Is that a good idea or just bonkers? Our writers weigh up the pros and cons

F1 had long planned to increase the number of sprints from the current six weekends per year because. The format allows promoters to offer their paying customers more on-track action that matters, making a sprint weekend an enticing proposition worth forking out money for. The numbers show fans also tune in more often than for meaningless practice sessions, even if the sprint format itself draws mixed review.
Has F1 taken things a step too far by applying the sprint format to Monaco's processional racetrack? Our writers issue their verdict.
Two qualifying sessions disrupt the DNA of the Monaco weekend build-up - Ronald Vording

I have to admit that I am still not the biggest fan of the sprint format, although perhaps a slightly less fervent opponent than I was a few years ago. You get used to everything, I suppose, although if given the choice I would still prefer a traditional race weekend – also partly because of the workflow for written media at the track.

Nevertheless, the commercial benefits of sprint weekends are clear. Fridays and Saturdays are made more attractive for promoters, as those buying a ticket get more action with sessions that actually matter. Of course, F1 management says it is based on data showing how much fans love it, but everyone knows that does not tell the entire story.

A sprint in Monaco does not seem commercially necessary, but in that respect it is important to remember that a sprint weekend is not just about having two races. Logically, the format also means two qualifying sessions, and that is precisely what tipped the balance for Monaco. In that respect, next year we will get the best that Monaco has to offer twice.

Sounds good, you might say, as qualifying in Monaco always has fans on the edge of their seats. But it takes away some of the charm of the Monaco weekend. After all, the Monaco race weekend is all about the gradual build-up towards the absolute highlight, one of the finest moments of the F1 season. It is about watching the drivers get a little closer to the walls with every practice session before that one climax on Saturday afternoon.

The latter is also clear to see when walking trackside – which is unrivalled in Monaco. While drivers deliberately leave some margin during the first practice session, a day later – towards the end of FP3 – you increasingly see them searching for the limit at places such as Piscine and Tabac. It is flirting with risk, a balancing act between building confidence and wanting too much, too soon. And it is a balancing act that can go wrong – just ask Max Verstappen, who crashed during final practice in 2018 and had to miss qualifying with a potentially race-winning car.

Building up the Monaco weekend from session to session, with that one peak on Saturday, is an art for the drivers and a joy to watch. And it is precisely that dynamic that is now changing. Next year, the build-up towards regular qualifying will be completely different because of a sprint race in the morning, while it also raises the question of how much risk drivers will be willing to take, given Saturday afternoon is all-important for the outcome of the weekend.

Two qualifying sessions in Monaco will undoubtedly be spectacular, but this changes the DNA of the Monaco weekend and the way drivers build it up – and I'm not sure the purist in me necessarily needed that to change.
F1 could be braver with its sprint race format and consider reverse grids - Oleg Karpov

Making an F1 calendar is not a trivial task, and while it’s a good habit in the modern world to bash those in charge, they’re actually doing a decent job with it. Formula 1's schedule is a good mix of historic venues - with the likes of Monza, Spa and Monaco still having their place - and unique new ones like Las Vegas and Miami, as the world championship does its best to capitalise on its growth in the United States.

Madrid was a good step too, with the idea of a street track in one of the European capitals - and it’s a shame the track itself didn’t live up to expectations. But if the local organisers really make an effort to solve the overtaking issue, that can still be a success in the future.
The Canadian Grand Prix will also host a sprint weekend in 2027

Overall, the 2027 schedule is well done, and it’s also a bit pointless to moan about the number of races, which has increased compared to the not-so-distant past. But as a global entertainment business competing with other major sporting events, this step is inevitable. As, probably, is a further increase in the number of races.

While I understand that the plan must be to increase the number of sprint races even further - and potentially to make every grand prix feature one - questions remain over whether the format is right. And at least to me, it feels like F1 could be a bit braver with it, offering something different to a “mini-grand prix” which is fitted into the schedule of a larger event. Essentially, in its current state it just doesn’t offer much apart from a little preview of what we’re about to see in the main event.

That format also makes sure those who are scoring the most points get another chance to score even more, increasing the gap to the rest of the field - so why not just make that event about the smaller teams and give them an opportunity? Yes, you guessed it, I’m talking about reverse grids - and to me, it could at least be under consideration to turn the format upside down, scrapping the additional qualifying altogether and allowing the grid to be formed by the championship order - in reverse.

We’d see Cadillac and Williams drivers trying to salvage a few more points in such races, and that would surely add another intrigue: how many places can the championship leaders still gain, starting from the back?

Artificial? For sure. But having purpose-built vehicles going around circuits isn’t very natural in the first place either. That wouldn’t touch the grand prix format itself, with the biggest points still awarded for the main event, but would at least offer something different, with a completely new intrigue to it.
F1 2027 calendar just proves sprint format needs a shake-up

Some time ago I wrote a column for sister website Autosport arguing for a shake-up of the sprint race format, and seeing the 10 venues selected for a sprint in 2027 has only reinforced that idea in my head.

The long and short of it is that if you are going to offer 10 sprint races per year, it needs to have a different look than the main grand prix. Strategic variance is the main driver of on-track action and overtaking, and a short pitstop-less race offers very little of it.

Why not try a one-lap qualifying shootout on sprint weekends, and run it in championship order. That means that, as it stands, Kimi Antonelli would go out first when track conditions are not at their best, with the Aston Martins and Cadillac going out last.

It's not as artificial as a full-blown reverse grid solution, which I am heavily opposed for sporting reasons. But it is a softer way to add jeopardy, while still allowing drivers and teams to make the difference. And the format would only be applied to the sprint grid, retaining the purity of the actual grand prix itself.
Could a one-lap qualifying format help make F1's sprints stand out?

As far as Monaco goes, to me this feels like F1 is waving the white flag on the grand prix as a motor race rather than a glorified parade. It's clear that the Monaco Grand Prix isn't going anywhere, and that the track will also stay as it is for the long term given the logistical constraints.

The dreadful two-stop experiment of 2025 didn't work, so it feels like F1 chiefs have just given up on making the grand prix work and are instead leaning into what Monaco does best, which is to offer two qualifying shootouts instead of one.
It's understandable from a promotional point of view, but if we're just accepting some of F1's races are going to be a write-off in advance, then it feels like something is fundamentally wrong.
Is adding more sprint races a good idea? And how could F1 improve the format? Have your say below

relatedItems.summaryEn: Liam Lawson says he 'doesn't understand' why the Azerbaijan Grand Prix stewards took no further action against Racing Bulls team-mate Arvid Lindblad, who spun him around during the race.
detailZh: 利亚姆·劳森：“我不明白”为什么阿尔维德·林德布拉德在撞坏我的底板后没有受到处罚
小红牛两名车手之间的碰撞，差点毁掉了车队原本意外取得的不错成绩
阿尔维德·林德布拉德，小红牛，利亚姆·劳森，小红牛
利亚姆·劳森表示，他“不明白”阿塞拜疆大奖赛的赛事干事为何没有对小红牛队友阿尔维德·林德布拉德采取进一步行动，后者在今天的F1比赛中把他撞得原地打转。
在亚历山大·阿尔本于巴库第30圈撞车退赛并引发安全车出动后，劳森和林德布拉德在比赛重启前分列第12位和第14位。
绿旗挥出后，弗兰科·科拉平托严重锁死车轮，把阿尔平队友加斯利和兰多·诺里斯都撞出了比赛。与此同时，林德布拉德比身前的劳森和埃斯特班·奥康刹车更晚，最终被夹在两车之间，并把队友的车撞得打转。
赛事干事认为这次碰撞是由于“林德布拉德可用的空间有限，以及前方事故引发的连锁反应”造成的，因此林德布拉德免于受罚——但劳森虽然在查看这次碰撞之前发表讲话，却并不完全认同这一结果。
这位新西兰车手回顾道：“进入1号弯时，我的加速出现严重迟滞，完全没有动力，所以埃斯特班就在我旁边。我试图给他留出空间，然后我左侧面被撞得非常猛，车底被撞出一个洞，之后我们就没什么办法再战斗了。我不太清楚到底发生了什么。”
“我一直尽量保持干净的驾驶，今年有些时候显然比较激进，但是……我不知道，进入1号弯时想从两辆车中间那样挤过去，我觉得本来就不太可能实现。”
利亚姆·劳森，小红牛；阿尔维德·林德布拉德，小红牛
当被问到干事的判罚对车队有利但对他本人不太有利时，劳森评论道：“对车队来说是好事。显然我不会去抗议我的队友，但是……
“我不理解这个判罚，因为我被撞得那么重，我的底板上都被撞出了一个洞。我当时只是在转向过弯，还给了对方空间。从我坐的位置来看我不理解，但可以说这对车队来说是好事。”
林德布拉德一有机会就向队友道了歉。他在媒体采访区再次表达了歉意，同时部分将这次事故归咎于埃斯特班·奥孔在刹车时移动路线——但录像画面并不支持这一说法。
这位新秀说：“从我那边的情况来看，我和埃斯特班在直道上已经这样交锋了大约三次，我们几次接近又刹车又再次加速，所以场面完全混乱，赛车的电池也因此在不太理想的工作区间。”
“然后大家在1号弯都刹车得稍微有点晚，我当时准备对埃斯特班完成超越，但他在最后一刻移动了路线，基本上就是在刹车时变线，所以我不得不采取躲避动作，这导致我的前轮轻微锁死，然后就撞上了利亚姆。”
“我在无线电上说了‘对不起’，但归根结底这不是故意的。如果你回看视频，就能看到我的动作没有任何故意成分。干事们判定‘不予进一步处罚’，我对此当然感到高兴，但说到底，我也不知道你想让我怎么做。如果我们都在极限边缘，大家都刹车得很晚，而我前面的车手在最后一秒移动了路线……当时有很多起事故。我什么也做不了，事情就是这样。”
林德布拉德补充说，小红牛告诉他：“我们看得出你其实没什么别的办法”，尽管他仍然预料到自己“会挨一点训斥”。
无论如何，对于这支总部位于法恩扎的车队来说还是有积极一面的——林德布拉德追回到第七名，以0.03秒的优势从奥康手中抢下了这个位置，而且阿尔派由于科拉平托的失误显然未能得分。这意味着在车队积分榜第五名的争夺中，理论上出现了13分的摆动，目前小红牛领先15分。
“从积极的角度看，我们作为一支车队拿到了积分。说实话，今天我们非常非常幸运，阿尔派没有得分，”劳森承认。“我们没有他们那样的速度。”
“某种意义上我们接受这个结果，因为这个周末我们挣扎了很多，这是本赛季我们第一次难以在排位赛第一节脱身，”林德布拉德表示赞同。“所以能成为除领先集团之外的最佳，并拿到大量积分，真是太棒了。这个周末并不轻松，但积分终究是在周日正赛里拿下的。”
林德布拉德本周日可能实际上拿不到任何积分，但他至少在周六把任务完成了。
detailEn: Liam Lawson: “I don’t understand” why Arvid Lindblad escaped penalty after wrecking my floor
A collision between the Racing Bulls jeopardised what turned out to be an unexpected decent result for the team
Arvid Lindblad, Racing Bulls, Liam Lawson, Racing Bulls
Liam Lawson says he ‘doesn’t understand’ Azerbaijan Grand Prix stewards took no further action against Racing Bulls team-mate Arvid Lindblad, who spun him around in today’s Formula 1 race.
After Alexander Albon crashed out on lap 30 in Baku, causing a safety car intervention, Lawson and Lindblad lay 12th and 14th ahead of the restart.

When the green flag was waved, Franco Colapinto had a massive lock-up and took both Alpine team-mate Pierre Gasly and Lando Norris out of the race. Meanwhile, Lindblad braked later than Lawson and Esteban Ocon ahead of him, ending up sandwiched between the two cars, and sent the sister car into a spin.

The stewards deemed the collision to have been caused by “the restricted space available to [Lindblad] and the chain reaction caused by the incident ahead”, hence Lindblad escaping a penalty – but Lawson, albeit speaking before reviewing the clash, didn’t quite agree with that outcome.

“Coming into Turn 1, I had massive boost lag and I didn’t have any power, so Esteban was next to me,” the New Zealander recounted. “I tried to give him space and then I just got hit from my left so hard that it put a hole on the floor, and we couldn’t really fight after that. I don’t really know what happened.

“I’ve always tried to keep clear, and it’s been obviously aggressive at points this year, but… I don't know, going into Turn 1 there to try and fit through the middle of two cars like that, I don't think it was ever really going to happen.”
Liam Lawson, Racing Bulls, Arvid Lindblad, Racing Bulls
Asked if the stewards’ decision was good for the team but not so much for him, Lawson commented: “Great for the team. Obviously I'm not going to go and protest my team-mate, but…

“I don't understand it, because I got hit so hard that it put a hole in my floor. I was just turning for the corner, giving the guy space. From where I'm sitting I don't understand, but let's say it's great for the team.”

Lindblad did apologise to his team-mate as soon as he got the opportunity to. He reiterated this in the media pen while partly blaming the incident on Esteban Ocon moving under braking – which the footage doesn’t corroborate.

“From where we were, me and Esteban, we'd gone about three times on the straight, we'd sort of gone and braked and gone again, so it was complete chaos, the battery wasn't in a good window because of that,” the rookie said.

“And then everyone braked a little bit too late in Turn 1, and I was going to make the move on Esteban and he moved in the last minute, basically moved under braking, so I had to take avoiding action, which meant I locked the front slightly and I hit Liam.

“I said ‘I'm sorry’ on the radio, but in the end it's not intentional. If you watch the video back you can see there's nothing intentional about what I do. The stewards said ‘no further action’, which obviously I'm happy about, but in the end, I don't know what you want me to do. If we're all on the limit, we all brake very late, and the guy in front of me moves in the last second… There were many incidents. There was nothing I could do, and it is what it is.”
Lindblad added that Racing Bulls told him, ‘We can see there's not much you could have done’, though he did expect to “get a little bit told off” still.

Regardless, there were silver linings for the Faenza-based outfit – Lindblad recovered to seventh, snatching that position away from Ocon by 0.03s, and Alpine obviously failed to score following Colapinto’s blunder. That represents a theoretical 13-point swing in their battle for fifth in the constructors’ championship, with Racing Bulls now 15 points ahead.
“On the positive, we scored points as a team. We got very, very lucky today that Alpine didn’t, honestly,” Lawson admitted. “We didn't have [their] speed.”

“We take the result, in a sense, because we've struggled a lot this weekend, it's been one of the first times this season we've struggled to get out of Q1,” Lindblad concurred. “So to be best of the rest and scoring massive points is absolutely amazing. It's not been an easy weekend, but points are scored on Sunday.”
Lindblad may not actually score any points this Sunday, but he did get the job done on Saturday after all.

relatedItems.originalTitle: "Mr Horner is looking for a job" – Frederic Vasseur claps back at Ferrari rumours
relatedItems.summaryEn: Ferrari team principal Frederic Vasseur has clapped back at speculation about his future, saying the rumours are distracting the team from its job. The speculation arose after Ferrari drifted into a competitive no-man's land, with Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton finishing fourth and sixth.
detailZh: “霍纳先生正在找工作”——弗雷德里克·瓦塞尔回击关于法拉利的传闻
法拉利车队领队弗雷德里克·瓦塞尔表示，关于他未来的猜测正在分散车队的注意力，使其无法专注于本职工作
弗雷德里克·瓦塞尔，法拉利车队领队兼总经理，与克里斯蒂安·霍纳，红牛车队领队
法拉利几乎是意大利的第二宗教——因此每当它未能实现其远大目标时，就会有传言称其领导层正面临威胁。
在2026年规则重置之后的季前测试和赛季初的比赛中展现出相当大的潜力之后，法拉利却滑入了竞争力上的无人区，夏尔·勒克莱尔正是这一困境的缩影
勒克莱尔和刘易斯·汉密尔顿分别以第四名和第六名完赛，与前方的赛车差距明显。车队目前在车队积分榜上排名第二，但大幅落后于梅赛德斯，并且受到迈凯伦和红牛的威胁。
汉密尔顿在巴塞罗那的胜利依然是本赛季的亮点，这也让法拉利在那些原本期望表现出色的赛道上令人失望的成绩显得更加刺眼。
在执行力方面一直存在持续的失误，例如在意大利大奖赛和阿塞拜疆的排位赛中，都没有为两辆赛车安排牵引助力，而汉密尔顿也多次批评车队缺乏纪律——不过这一点应放在他希望车队支持他那日渐黯淡的夺冠雄心的背景下看待。
这不可避免地让车队的领导层受到审视，尽管瓦塞尔的合同一直延续到2027年底，但他仍被关于其前途的传闻所困扰。
最近几天这些传闻愈演愈烈，不过据了解，所谓他正在被“安排”逐步退居二线的说法，其实并非来自法拉利内部。
但它们究竟从何而来？毫无疑问是出自某个带有自己目的的消息源——或者，正如这类事情的常见情形一样，来自那些没有其他法拉利相关要闻可写的意大利网站。
最近这轮猜测的爆发，恰逢前红牛车队领队克里斯蒂安·霍纳接受《泰晤士报》采访，为其下月出版的新回忆录做宣传。在采访中，他承认，想要获得公司的股权，是他回归一个重要职位的前提条件。
“我在维修区墙上坐了21年，我不需要再回到那种日子……在我人生的这个阶段，只有一支车队会让我愿意接受不参与所有权的情况。”
“我会考虑法拉利吗？我是说，法拉利是F1中最大的品牌。它是梦想，也可以说是F1中的沉睡巨人。”
在阿塞拜疆大奖赛后被问及关于他职位的持续猜测是否给车队带来了压力时，瓦塞尔以他惯常的那种令人放松又略带调侃的方式回应。
“如果问题是这个的话，我们的工作环境并不是完全平静的。”他如是说道。
“对我来说，首先是这一点，对车队里的每个人、对媒体、对围绕这件事的50%的提问来说，我认为这是一个多少令人沮丧的局面。
“我们正在为年度第二名而战。说到底，我们大家都在谈论很多关于这件事（关于他位置的传闻），甚至连维修区里的技师们也在讨论这个，这不是我们能进行的最好的讨论。但事实就是如此，这不在我的掌控之中。
“霍纳先生正在找工作——这一点众所周知——到处在找。
“但我能做什么呢？我只能尽力推动车队，要求他们保持斗志，专注于今天什么才是最有利的，而不是把时间花在八卦上。
“但每次采访都是如此，一天大概25次，我想我们又在回到这个话题上。”
F1媒体往往像一个回音室，尤其是在赛季的这个阶段，关于车手下赛季转会的猜测已经成为一个被谈论到 被榨干、毫无新意的话题。
一条小小的传闻经过无休止的重复，就可能演变成近乎事实的东西。
夏尔·勒克莱尔，法拉利，弗雷德里克·瓦塞尔，法拉利
但法拉利在短时间内与领导者分道扬镳这件事上是有前科的。瓦塞尔本人就是在马蒂亚·比诺托之后被任命上位的，后者在2022年底‘辞职’，而那个赛季法拉利的局面同样是竞争力逐渐流失。当一个项目被认为正在失败时，往往需要一个替罪羊。
霍纳本人对此深有体会——在他的回忆录中，他把被赶下台归因于迪特里希·马特希茨去世后红牛内部权力更迭所引发的内斗，加上一段竞争力的统治期戛然而止。
在《泰晤士报》的采访中，他承认自己是一个“两极分化的角色”（Marmite character），尽管他拥有成功的履历。
当被问及下赛季是否会回到F1围场时，他说：“我不知道。我既是解药，也是问题。”
现任法拉利车队领队正因有关其前途的问题被各方穷追猛打，而那位悠闲的绅士则在牛津郡一栋二级保护豪宅的惬意环境中观望机会，两者之间形成了耐人寻味的对比。
他说：“我的处境非常优越，可以挑剔着选。”
“就算我什么都不做，也可以在这个房子里度过余生，只需要操心会不会下雨、草能不能长绿。”
“但这样能满足我吗？不能。我仍然觉得还有一支舞要跳。托托也需要把头发再揉乱一回了。”
detailEn: "Mr Horner is looking for a job" – Frederic Vasseur claps back at Ferrari rumours
Ferrari team principal Frederic Vasseur says speculation about his future is distracting his team from its job
Frederic Vasseur, Team Principal and General Manager, Scuderia Ferrari, with Christian Horner, Team Principal, Red Bull Racing
Ferrari is practically Italy’s second religion – so whenever it falls short of its lofty ambitions, speculation follows that its leaders are under threat.
After showing considerable promise in the pre-season and early races following the 2026 rules reset, Ferrari has drifted into a competitive no-man’s land epitomised by Charles

Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton finishing fourth and sixth, distant from the cars ahead. It is second in the constructors’ championship, but well behind Mercedes and under threat from McLaren and Red Bull.
Hamilton’s win in Barcelona remains the season’s bright spot, and one that throws disappointing results at circuits where Ferrari expected to excel into even sharper relief.

There have been persistent slips in execution, such as not orchestrating a tow for both cars in qualifying for the Italian GP and again in Azerbaijan, and Hamilton has repeatedly criticised the lack of discipline – though this should be viewed in the context of him wanting the team to support his fading championship ambitions.
This had inevitably brought the team’s leadership under scrutiny and Vasseur has been dogged by rumours about his future, even though his contract extends to the end of 2027.
These have intensified in recent days, though it’s understood that claims he is being “stage managed” into retirement are not actually sourced from within Ferrari.
But where do they come from? Indubitably a source with an agenda – or, as is often the way with such things, Italian websites with few other Ferrari-based matters of moment to discuss.

The latest burst of speculation coincides with an interview former Red Bull team principal Christian Horner gave to The Times to promote his new memoir, which is published next month. In it, he acknowledged that his desire to have equity in the business has been a prerequisite for him returning to a leading role.
“I did 21 years sitting on the pitwall. I don’t need to go back to that… At this stage in my life, there’s only one team for which I would accept non-participation in ownership.
“Would I consider Ferrari? I mean, Ferrari is the biggest brand in Formula 1. It’s the dream and arguably it’s the sleeping giant of Formula 1.”
Asked after the Azerbaijan Grand Prix whether the constant speculation about his position was putting the team under pressure, Vasseur responded in his usual disarmingly wry fashion.
“We are not working in perfect serenity, if that is the question,” he said.
“For me, first, but for everybody on the team, for the media, for 50% of the questions about this, I think it's a bit of a frustrating situation.

“We are fighting for P2 in the championship. At the end of the day, we are all speaking a lot about this [rumours about his position], and even for the guys in the garage to discuss about this, it's not the best discussion that we can have. But it is what it is, it's not in my hands.
“Mr Horner is looking for a job – that everybody knows – everywhere.
“But what can I do? Just to try to do my best to push the team, to ask them to be motivated, focus on what is better today, and not to spend time with gossips.
“But each interview, it's been 25 times a day, I think we are coming back on this.”
The F1 media tends to act as an echo chamber, especially at a time in the season when speculation about driver moves for the coming season has become an exhausted subject.
A single piece of scuttlebutt can metamorphose into something adjacent to fact through endless repetition.
Charles Leclerc, Ferrari, Frederic Vasseur, Ferrari

But Ferrari has form in parting with leaders at short notice. Vasseur himself was installed in place of Mattia Binotto, who ‘resigned’ at the end of 2022, a season in which Ferrari’s narrative was similarly one of competitive drift. A human sacrifice is often required when a project is deemed to be failing.

Horner himself knows this well enough – in his memoir he ascribes his ousting to internal politics surrounding the regime change at Red Bull following the death of Dietrich Mateschitz, combined with a run of competitive dominance coming to an abrupt end.
In his interview in The Times he acknowledged that he is a “Marmite character”, albeit one with a track record of success.
Asked if he would be back in the F1 paddock next season, he said: “I don’t know. I’m the cure and the problem.”

There is a fascinating contrast between the present occupant of the Ferrari team principal role, battered from all sides about questions regarding his future, and the gentleman of leisure keeping his options open from the convivial environs of his Grade II listed Oxfordshire mansion.
“I’m in a very fortunate position that I can afford to be picky,” he said.
“If I don’t do anything, I can live here for whatever time I’ve got left on the planet, and just worry about whether it’s going to rain and make the grass green or not.
“But is that going to fulfil me? No. I still feel that there’s another dance. And Toto needs to have his hair f***ing ruffled up.”

relatedItems.originalTitle: Winners and losers from F1's Azerbaijan Grand Prix street brawl
relatedItems.summaryEn: The Azerbaijan Grand Prix in Baku was a race of two halves, with a bland opening transformed by a pair of mid-race safety cars and chaos at the lap 36 restart. The melee expanded the list of losers while producing several unlikely winners.
detailZh: F1阿塞拜疆大奖赛街头混战中的赢家与输家
看起来像是在巴库街道上的一场相对无聊的巡游，最终演变成了一场充满混乱的街头混战。以下是我们评选出的F1阿塞拜疆大奖赛的赢家与输家
弗朗哥·科拉平托，阿尔派；兰多·诺里斯，迈凯伦
这不是巴库第一次成为“上下半场截然不同”的比赛的典型。平淡无味的主菜，配上一道由比赛中段两次安全车引发的大快朵颐的甜点。随着一脚刹车轻点，第36圈重启时的混战让输家阵营的候选人数翻倍，而赢家名单上则涌现出不少意想不到的英雄。
由于两次安全车重启，事情比计划中要刺激得多，但这个周末属于拉塞尔。他从始至终气势如虹，杆位发车一路领跑到终点夺冠，还顺带拿下了大满贯。
对安东内利来说，这是一个混乱的周末，一部分是他自己造成的，另一部分则是因为缺乏赛道时间让这位意大利车手处于劣势，而拉塞尔重新找回了本赛季的最佳状态。
是为时已晚，还是恰逢其时地开启一场意外的赛季末逆袭？这可能更多取决于安东内利而不是拉塞尔，因为差距仍然高达66分。但无论拉塞尔此前需要解决什么问题才能与2026年赛车合拍，如今已经开始奏效了。
"我认为这主要是因为我对这种新采用的驾驶风格有了更多经验。休赛期之后的每一场比赛，我都感觉自己越来越强，也越来越像原来的自己。这段时间对我来说非常艰难，但我感觉自己已经走出来了。"
比撞上自己队友更糟糕的事，就是连同队友一起把无辜的旁观者也带出局。周六晚上，阿尔派（阿尔派）车队上下心情沉重：车队为争夺第五名的战斗中辛苦追回的地盘，随着皮埃尔·加斯利的侧箱一瞬间灰飞烟灭。
弗朗哥·科拉平托在巴库的失误甚至招致了另一位受害者、世界冠军兰多·诺里斯的呼声，要求对他实施禁赛。这本可以算作一时冲动的言论，如果不是这位迈凯伦车手在混合区来回走动时反复说了好几次的话。
这是诺里斯在度过一个令人沮丧的下午之后的一点轻微过激反应吗？也许吧。但你多少会感觉到，科拉平托的大老板弗拉维奥·布里亚托利也不太满意……
“我知道弗朗哥已经承担了全部责任，这是他应该做的；事实上，考虑到比赛当时的局面和安全车重启的情况，他刹车刹得太晚了。以他这种经验水平的车手来说，这是一个非常糟糕的操作。”
弗拉维奥。他说话向来不留情面，也常常“压榨”他的车手。
迈凯伦车队领队、同为意大利人的安德烈亚·斯特拉说得最妙：“我猜这会由干事审查，我也确信弗拉维奥也会审查这件事。我不确定哪边会更严厉……”
鉴于科拉平托本赛季表现出色，足以赢得2027年的续约，巴库的事件很可能会被原谅。但了解布里亚托雷的人都知道，这事不会被遗忘。
赢家：塞尔吉奥·佩雷斯 / 输家：瓦尔特利·博塔斯
是塞尔吉奥·佩雷兹真的太出色，还是瓦尔特利·博塔斯只是表现平平？两位凯迪拉克车手之间这种没有其他原因可以解释的巨大表现差距，说明两方面原因都占了不小的比重。
佩雷兹从巴库一开始就令人着迷，重新找回了他“街道赛之王”的旧日威名，把他的凯迪拉克带到了这辆车本不配达到的位置。当博塔斯毫无速度可言时，佩雷兹在第一节段里能与两辆奥迪周旋，很快就拉开了对队友一次进站所需的差距，到第28圈博塔斯驶入维修区时，这个差距已经膨胀到了52秒。
能够跟在加布里埃尔·博托莱托以及随后卡洛斯·塞恩斯的尾流里——因此处于超车模式的激活窗口内——在一段时间里帮了佩雷兹的忙，但这并不能解释两人之间如此悬殊的表现差距。
“这是我在巴库最好的周末之一，我把那辆车的潜力发挥到了150%，”佩雷兹说。“由于有超车模式，我们在和一些比我们快一两秒的赛车战斗，所以整个第一节段我们都能咬住他们。”与此同时，博塔斯表示，在只能和阿斯顿·马丁的费尔南多·阿隆索缠斗之后，他必须去寻找答案。人们希望他能找到一些。
伊萨克·哈贾尔（哈贾尔）在伤愈复出后庆祝了自己可能代表红牛至今最强的一场比赛表现，其出色程度丝毫不逊于他去年在赞德沃特夺得首个大奖赛领奖台时的发挥。
哈贾尔忍着左手腕骨裂的伤痛，排位赛位列第四并最终收获第三名，在使用更占优势的软胎时与队友马克斯·维斯塔潘（维斯塔潘）不相上下。以至于在第一次安全车出动之前，这位法国车手正准备尝试向队友发起进攻。
哈贾尔因拳击受伤被迫缺席三周，这对他的持续成长来说非常不利，但这位好斗的21岁车手证明了自己并没有不堪一击的软肋。
诺里斯完全有理由对科拉平托（Colapinto）感到愤怒，考虑到他的收件箱很可能被辱骂信息淹没，明智的做法是再次暂停使用社交媒体。但事实是，他本就不该处在会被中游车手撞出比赛的境地。以他在2026年的高标准来看，诺里斯度过了一个相当糟糕的周末，因为迈凯伦在低速性能和空气动力学效率方面的欠缺在巴库赛道被暴露得尤为严重。
尽管经历了这一切，奥斯卡·皮亚斯特里仍然排位第三，而且看起来很有登上领奖台的价值，直到他和诺里斯一样在1号弯刹车过头，正是这次失误让诺里斯在安全车出动前掉入了车阵中游。
那么，诺里斯到底出了什么问题？车队领队斯特拉解释说，这位英国车手一直在应对一个间歇性的燃油喷射问题，这个问题在排位赛和正赛中都损失了诺里斯的直线速度，同时车队也没能解决能量部署的难题。但诺里斯也主动承认了自己的问题。“以我当时拥有的速度，我在赛道上毫无机会，但我确信自己在驾驶方面有些地方做得还不够好，”他说。“我需要看看下次能改进些什么。”
塞尔吉奥·佩雷斯和埃斯特班·奥孔在巴库度过了一个积极的周末。弗兰科·科拉平托则不然。
这是一个今年在这里不常出现的名字，而巴库是一个来之不易的将功补过的机会。
一段时间以来，奥孔在哈斯已经一只脚踏出车门，这早已是公开的秘密。而在巴库大奖赛周末之前，他另一只脚也随之迈了出去——这位法国车手公开宣布自己是“自由身”。在众多候选人中，据了解，法拉利青训体系出身的拉斐尔·卡马拉（Rafael Camara）最近在波尔蒂芒（Portimao）的一次测试中令车队眼前一亮。
明知自己待的时间不多了，而车队已经为2027年找到了更心仪的人选，还要在这样的情况下在F1中力争表现，会是什么滋味？我们永远无从知晓。但对奥孔来说，这一切肯定不好受——他要在一辆时好时坏、只偶尔能让你展现价值的赛车上为职业生涯而战。
不过在巴库，奥孔的VF-26赛车表现没有任何异常。而且在他凭借机会主义从队友奥利·贝尔曼手中抢下第八名之后，他还在新闻媒体面前毫不示弱地为自己据理力争。
“我可以说这是我应得的，而不是其余那些破事。我和场上所有人都交过手，我一直都不逊色于任何人。我参加过每个系列赛都拿过冠军。我赢过三级方程式，我赢过GP3，我赢过F1。我做到了，你明白吗？我是场上最出色的车手之一，而且我不怕这么说。”
阿斯顿·马丁在匈牙利带来大规模升级后所抱有的任何希望，如今似乎都已破灭。本田随后的动力单元升级或许改善了一些领域，但仍与竞争对手相差甚远。
如果说有什么变化，那就是赛车的可靠性和可操控性似乎是倒退而非前进：兰斯·斯特罗尔已连续四场大奖赛退赛，费尔南多·阿隆索也不断受到各种问题的困扰。
但最明显的差距仍在性能方面：在巴库的长直道上，阿隆索和斯特罗尔的速度 routinely 落后梅赛德斯多达30公里每小时。
本田的困境引发了进一步的争论：随着国际汽联的追赶机制（ADUO）即将进行新的调整，本田是否应该获得规则上的更多帮助。但由于本田在今年早些时候已经获得了额外的研发余量，它必须最迟在2027年就展示出重大进步。
detailEn: Winners and losers from F1's Azerbaijan Grand Prix street brawl
What looked like a relatively boring parade down the streets of Baku turned into a chaos-filled street brawl. Here are our winners and losers from F1's eventful Azerbaijan GP
Franco Colapinto, Alpine, Lando Norris, McLaren

Not for the first time, Baku was the epitome of a race of two halves. A flavourless main course washed down with an indulgent dessert, triggered by a mid-race pair of safety cars. With one dab of the brake pedal, the lap 36 restart melee doubled the number of candidates for the loser category, while the list of winners boasts a number of unlikely heroes.

Things got a lot spicier than planned courtesy of the brace of safety car restarts, but this was George Russell's weekend. Imperious from start to finish with a pole-to-flag victory and a grand slam to boot.
On a messy weekend for Kimi Antonelli, partly due to his own making and partly because a lack of track time left the Italian on the back foot, Russell reconnected with his best form this season.

Too little too late, or just in time for an unexpected late-season comeback? That will likely depend more on Antonelli than on Russell, with the gap still a sizeable 66 points. But whatever Russell needed to address to hit his stride with the 2026 cars, it is starting to click.

"I think it’s just having more experience with this sort of new driving style I’ve adopted. And every race since the break, I feel like I’ve gone from strength to strength and I feel like more myself again. It’s been a really tough period for me, but I feel like I’ve come through the other side."

The only thing worse than crashing into your team-mate is taking out innocent bystanders with him. Alpine was not a happy camp to be in on Saturday night after all the hard work the team did to reclaim ground in the battle for fifth disappeared with one fell swoop into Pierre Gasly's sidepod.

Franco Colapinto's Baku blunder even prompted calls from his other victim, world champion Lando Norris, for a race ban. That could be classified as a heat of the moment comment, if it hadn't been for the fact the McLaren driver repeated it a number of times as he roamed the mixed zone.
A slight overreaction after a frustrating afternoon for Norris? Perhaps. But you somehow get the impression Colapinto's big boss Flavio Briatore wasn't all that impressed either...

"I know that Franco has taken full responsibility for it, as he should; in fact he braked far too late considering the context of the race and the safety car restart. It was a very poor move for a driver of his experience."
Flav. Never one to mince his words, often one to mince his drivers.

McLaren team boss and fellow Italian Andrea Stella said it best. "I guess this is being reviewed by the stewards and I'm sure it will be reviewed by Flavio as well. I'm not sure which one is going to be harsher..."
With Colapinto having impressed enough this season to earn a 2027 extension, the Baku incident will likely be forgiven. But knowing Briatore, it will not be forgotten.
Winner: Sergio Perez / Loser Valtteri Bottas
Was Sergio Perez simply outstanding or Valtteri Bottas just lacklustre? The otherwise unexplained chasm in performance between the two Cadillac drivers suggests it's a healthy serving of both.

Perez was mesmerising from the outset in Baku, reconnecting with his old reputation for being a street circuit monster, and putting his Cadillac up where it didn't deserve to be. As Bottas was bereft of pace, Perez entertained the company of the Audis during the first stint, soon pulling out a pitstop gap on his team-mate which ballooned to 52 seconds by the time Bottas peeled into the pits on lap 28.
Being able to stay in Gabriel Bortoleto's and then Carlos Sainz's slipstream - and thus Overtake Mode window - helped Perez for a while, but doesn't explain the huge gulf in performance.

"It's been one of my best weekends in Baku, I managed to get 150% out of that car," Perez said. "We were fighting cars that are a second or two seconds faster than us, due to the overtake mode so we stayed with them throughout the first stint." Meanwhile, Bottas said he would have to look for answers after only being able to fight Aston Martin's Fernando Alonso. One hopes he finds a couple.

Isack Hadjar celebrated his return from his injury layoff with what is likely his strongest performance for Red bull to date, and every bit as impressive as his maiden grand prix podium in Zandvoort last year.

Nursing a fractured left wrist, Hadjar qualified fourth and finished third and proved a match for team-mate Max Verstappen on the favoured soft tyres. So much so that the Frenchman was poised to try and attack his team-mate right before the first safety car came out.
Hadjar's enforced three-week absence following his boxing injury was most unwelcome for his continuing development, but the pugnacious 21-year-old showed he doesn't have a glass jaw.

Norris has every right to be upset with Colapinto, and he would be wise to take another social media sabbatical with his inbox likely flooded with abuse. But the truth is he should never have been in a position to be taken out by midfielders to begin with. Norris has had a particularly poor weekend by his high 2026 standards as McLaren's lack of low-speed performance and aero efficiency hit particularly hard in Baku.

But despite all that, Oscar Piastri still qualified third and looked good value for a podium until he joined Norris in outbraking himself into Turn 1, the transgression that dumped Norris into the midfield before the safety car.

So, what was going on with Norris? Team principal Stella explained the Briton had been dealing with an intermittent fuel injection problem that cost Norris straightline performance both in qualifying and the race, while the team didn't nail its energy deployment puzzle. But Norris also held his hand up. "I had no chance out there with the speed I had, but I'm sure there were some things I wasn't doing well enough in driving," he said. "I need to see what I can improve for next time."
Sergio Perez and Esteban Ocon enjoyed a positive Baku weekend. Franco Colapinto, not so much.
Now there's a name that hasn't featured here very often this year, and Baku was a hard-earned opportunity to make amends.

It has been an open secret for a while that Ocon has had one foot out the door at Haas. Ahead of the Baku weekend, it emerged his other foot had joined suit as the Frenchman declared himself a "free agent". Among a pool of candidates, Ferrari junior Rafael Camara is understood to have dazzled the team during a recent test outing at Portimao.

What is it like trying to perform in F1 knowing you're on borrowed time and your team has found more desirable options for 2027? We will never know. But it can't have been easy for Ocon to deal with, trying to fight for your career aboard in an inconsistent car that only occasionally allows you to show your worth.
But In Baku, Ocon's VF-26 performed without any anomalies. And after he opportunistically snatched eighth away from team-mate Ollie Bearman, he defiantly fought his corner in the press, too.

"I can say I deserve that, not all the rest of the shit. I've raced with everyone out there and I've always been on par. I've won in every championship that I've raced in. I won Formula 3. I won GP3. I won in Formula 1. I can do it, you know? I'm one of the best out there, and I'm not afraid to say it."

Any hopes Aston Martin harboured after its sizeable Hungary upgrade now seem to have vanished. Honda's subsequent power unit upgrade may have improved some areas, but it is still miles away from the competition.

If anything, the car's reliability and driveability appears to have taken a step back rather forward, with Lance Stroll retiring from his fourth straight grand prix and Fernando Alonso continuously plagued by problems, too.
But the most striking deficit remains on the performance front, as Alonso and Stroll routinely shipped up to 30km/h on Baku's long straight compared to Mercedes.

Honda's plight has triggered further debate over whether it deserves more assistance from the regulations as the FIA's ADUO catch-up mechanism is set for fresh tweaks. But with Honda already afforded extra development headroom earlier this year, it must demonstrate a major step forward as early as 2027.
